homeIntro: HARU turns a few clips from your phone into a short film, with music made for HARU, subtitles, your name and logo. Everything is made on your phone: your videos are never sent to us.
supportIntro: A question about HARU, an idea or something that does not work? Write to us and tell us your phone model and the version of HARU (About HARU, on the home screen).
supportDataBody: HARU has no account and keeps your drafts and films on your phone. To remove them, delete them in HARU or delete the app. Films you saved to Photos or shared stay where you put them.
sourcesIntro: HARU makes its films with FFmpeg, which is free software licensed under the GNU Lesser General Public License 3.0 or later (LGPL). HARU itself is not open source; the LGPL lets it use FFmpeg on these terms. Here is the complete source code of the FFmpeg libraries in HARU, and how to build them.
sourcesCarriesBody: HARU 1.0.45 and later, on Android and iPhone: FFmpeg 8.1.2, built by FFmpegKit as separate shared libraries (libavcodec, libavdevice, libavfilter, libavformat, libavutil, libswresample, libswscale and ffmpegkit). The “min” build: no GPL or non-free part. FFmpeg is not modified.
sourcesFilesNote: The archives and licence texts below are the originals, in English.
sourcesBuildBody: Unpack the FFmpegKit archive and run ./build-all.sh android min or ./build-all.sh ios min (Android NDK 29.0.13113456, Xcode with the iOS SDK). The scripts fetch FFmpeg 8.1.2 and cpu_features from the same tags as the archives above; the exact FFmpeg configuration is printed by the libraries themselves (avutil_configuration()). The build takes hours and needs the full toolchain.
sourcesUseBody: The libraries are separate files inside the app: lib/<abi>/lib*.so on Android, Frameworks/*.framework on iPhone. You may replace them with your own build of FFmpeg 8.1.2 or a compatible version. If you need anything else from us to do so, write to us.
sourcesOfferBody: For at least three years after the last version of HARU that contains these libraries, we will send this source code to anyone who asks, for no more than the cost of sending it. Write to {mail}.
